info.name: Modeefe Mobile API — User
info.description:
API collection for the Modeefe mobile app.

**Scope: end-user (customer) only.** This app has no vendor, admin, or guide-account surface — every endpoint here is meant for a plain registered customer. `POST /auth/register` already hardcodes new accounts to the `user_role` setting (customer) server-side regardless of what the client sends, so there is no way to self-register as anything else through this API. `POST /auth/login` now also actively rejects vendor/guide/admin accounts with a clear error, so this API can't be reached as anything but a customer. (The Guide folder below is the one exception to "no guide surface" — it lets a customer *browse* guide profiles, same as Tour lets them browse tours; it has nothing to do with a guide managing their own account.)

**Booking requires registration + verification too.** Both Login and every write action under the Booking folder (Add to Cart, Add Enquiry, Checkout) reject unverified accounts with an `email_not_verified` error, so a user must be registered, logged in, and have clicked their email verification link before they can book a tour.

**Folders:** Auth (register, login, profile, password), Wishlist, Booking History, Tour (search/filters/detail/availability/reviews), Guide (search/filters/detail — browsing only), Car (search/filters/detail/availability/reviews), Event (search/filters/detail/availability/reviews), Shop (search/filters/detail/reviews), Booking (add to cart, enquiry, single-item checkout, status), Cart & Checkout (view cart, coupon, unified multi-item checkout, receipt, order history). Tickets/QR and profile deletion aren't included yet.

All requests are relative to the `base_url` collection variable. After a successful Login, the response's `access_token` is captured automatically into the `access_token` collection variable so subsequent authenticated requests (e.g. `Me`, `Logout`) can reuse it via the collection's Bearer Token auth.

request.description:
Creates a new customer account.

**Required:** `first_name`, `last_name`, `email` (unique), `password`, `term`.
**Optional:** `phone`.

The new user is always assigned the `user_role` setting's role (plain customer) server-side — the request body has no field that can influence this, so registering as a vendor/guide/admin isn't possible through this endpoint.

Gated by the `is_enable_registration()` site setting — if registration is disabled, this always returns the "You are not allowed to register" error regardless of input.

response.name: 200 — Registration disabled

exec: // Auto-capture the token so every other request in this collection
// (Bearer auth set at the collection level) can reuse it immediately.

request.description:
Authenticates a user and issues a Sanctum personal access token.

**Required:** `email`, `password`, `device_name` (used as the token's name — Sanctum lets a user hold one token per device, e.g. "iphone-14-abc123").

Only plain customer accounts (role matches the `user_role` setting, and not a guide) can obtain a token here — vendor/guide/admin accounts get a clear "account type isn't supported" error instead. The role check runs strictly after the password check, so a wrong password looks identical regardless of account type (no account-type enumeration via this endpoint).

Also requires a verified email, matching the website's own `middleware(['auth','verified'])` on the whole `/user/*` area — an unverified account can't get a token here either, so it can't reach full profile/wishlist/booking access through the mobile app while the website itself still has it walled off behind `/email/verify`.

response.name: 200 — Account type not allowed (vendor/guide/admin)
200 — Email not verified

request.description:
Returns the authenticated user's profile. Requires the Bearer token from Login (inherited from the collection's auth settings).

Adds `avatar_url`/`avatar_thumb_url` to the response only when the user has an `avatar_id` set.

Updates the authenticated user's profile.

**Required:** `first_name`, `last_name`, `email` (must stay unique).
**Also accepted:** any other fillable User field (e.g. `phone`, `address`, `birthday`, `gender`, `bio`), since the controller mass-assigns the whole request body.

⚠️ Caveat found while documenting this: the controller unconditionally does `date('Y-m-d', strtotime($user->birthday))` after filling, even when `birthday` isn't in the request at all. If the account has no birthday set yet, `strtotime('')` returns `false`, and this silently writes `1970-01-01` into `birthday` on *any* profile update, not just ones that intended to change it. Not fixed here since it's outside what was asked — flagging it for a follow-up.

Changes the authenticated user's password.

**Required:** `current_password`, `new_password` (min 6 characters).

All of the user's existing Sanctum tokens are revoked on success (including the one used for this request) — the client must log in again afterward, which is exactly what the `need_relogin` code in the response is signaling.
Revokes only the current access token (the one used to authenticate this request), not every token the user holds — unlike Change Password, other devices stay logged in.
Exchanges the current token for a fresh one. Call it when a request fails with 401 rather than sending the user back to the login screen.
Emails a 6-digit numeric reset token to the given address (if the account exists) for use with Reset Password.

Resets the password using the token emailed by Forgot Password.

**Required:** `email`, `token`, `password` (min 6, must be confirmed via `password_confirmation`).

The token expires after `config('auth.passwords.users.expire')` minutes — an expired or already-used token returns the same "invalid" error either way.

Confirms the account whose verification email linked here. No Bearer token needed/possible — a freshly-registered mobile user has no way to authenticate until verified, so this proves identity independently via the same id/hash/expires/signature the emailed link's signed URL already carries (`http://.../email/verify/{id}/{hash}?expires=...&signature=...`) — the mobile app just needs to parse those 4 values out of the link/deep-link and POST them here instead of opening it in a browser (which would hit a login wall, since that web route requires a session).

Rate-limited to 6 requests/minute, same as the web version.
Re-sends the verification email/link. Same no-token-needed reasoning as Verify Email — just an `email` lookup, same pattern as Forgot Password. Rate-limited to 6 requests/minute.

item.name: Account

request.description:
Returns the authenticated user straight from the token guard.

Note this is NOT /auth/me — it is Laravel's default sanctum route and returns the raw user model with no profile shaping. Prefer /auth/me in the app; this is useful for confirming a token is valid.

Irreversibly deletes the account and everything authored by it — services, bookings and media.

Gated by the `user_enable_permanently_delete` setting: if that is off, the call does nothing. Also disabled in demo mode.

Uploads a file and returns the media record whose id other endpoints accept (avatars, listing images).

Send as multipart/form-data with the file in `file`. Requires sanctum auth and upload permission on the account.

request.description: Tickets belonging to the signed-in customer, across all their bookings.

The QR image for one of the customer's tickets.

Returns an image, not JSON — render it directly rather than parsing the body.
Tickets sold against the signed-in vendor's own listings — the door list.

Marks a ticket as used at the door. Path is /scan/{booking_id}/{ticket_id}.

`code` is the value encoded in the customer's QR and is required — the booking and ticket ids alone are not enough to admit someone.

Returns an error message rather than a 4xx when the code does not match, so check the response body, not just the status.

Required — pixel size, numeric

request.description:
Renders any string as a QR image. Both parameters are required; `size` must be numeric.

item.description:
Two sides of the same feature. 'My Tickets' is the customer's own tickets with their QR images. 'Manage Tickets' is the vendor side: the tickets sold against their listings, and the scan endpoint used at the door.

All endpoints require a bearer token.

request.description: Bookable dates for this tour within `start`..`end` (both required) — use this to drive a date picker before calling Add to Cart, since Add to Cart will reject a `start_date` this doesn't consider available.

Requires the Login Bearer token — unlike the browse endpoints above, this needs an authenticated (registered) user.

**Fields are `review_title` + `review_content`, not `rate_number`/`content`.** This site has `tour_review_stats` configured (Service/Organization/Friendliness/Area Expert/Safety), so a tour review is scored per-category via `review_stats` (object keyed by category title, 1-5 each) — the average becomes the rating. A flat `review_rate` is only used as a fallback when a module has no stat categories configured (see Shop's Write a Review, which has none).

request.description: Per-day price/availability for this car within `start`..`end` (both required) — use this to drive the rental date-range picker before Add to Cart, which rejects a `start_date`/`end_date` this doesn't consider available.

Requires the Login Bearer token — unlike the browse endpoints above, this needs an authenticated (registered) user.

**Fields are `review_title` + `review_content`, not `rate_number`/`content`.** This site has `car_review_stats` configured (Equipment/Comfortable/Climate Control/Facility/Aftercare), so a car review is scored per-category via `review_stats` (object keyed by category title, 1-5 each) — the average becomes the rating.

item.description:
The Car listing/detail endpoints reuse the exact same generic `SearchController` as Tour (`{type}` = car) — these requests just pin `{type}` to `car`. None of these require auth; they're public browse/search endpoints.

**Booking a car differs from booking a tour**: instead of a single `start_date` + `guests`, Add to Cart for a car takes a rental **date range** (`start_date` + `end_date`, both `Y-m-d`) plus `number` (how many of this car — defaults to 1). Total is priced per day across the range. See Booking > Add to Cart for the shared endpoint; swap its example body's `service_type` to `"car"` and its date fields to this shape.

response.name: 200 — Success

request.description:
Requires the Login Bearer token — unlike the browse endpoints above, this needs an authenticated (registered) user.

**Fields are `review_title` + `review_content`, not `rate_number`/`content`.** This site has `event_review_stats` configured (Service/Organization/Friendliness/Area Expert/Safety), so an event review is scored per-category via `review_stats` (object keyed by category title, 1-5 each) — the average becomes the rating.

item.description:
The Event listing/detail endpoints reuse the exact same generic `SearchController` as Tour/Car/Guide (`{type}` = event) — these requests just pin `{type}` to `event`. None of these require auth; they're public browse/search endpoints.

**Booking an event differs from booking a tour/car**: the site currently runs `event_booking_type = "ticket"` (an admin setting, could instead be `"time_slot"` site-wide), so Add to Cart takes `start_date` (must be one of Event Availability's dates) plus a `ticket_types` object keyed by **array index** into the event's ticket tiers, e.g. `{ "0": { "number": 2 }, "1": { "number": 1 } }` to book 2 of ticket_types[0] and 1 of ticket_types[1]. There's no `guests` field — the ticket quantities themselves determine `total_guests`. See Booking > Add to Cart for the shared endpoint.

item.description:
Physical products ("Shop" in the storefront UI, `product_route_prefix` setting, default `/shop`). Reuses the generic `SearchController`/`BookingController` (`{type}=product`) — same engine as Tour/Car/Event — but products are the odd one out: no location, no dates/availability, and stock/variations instead of a booking calendar.

**Add to Cart is simpler than every other module**: `{ "service_id": 16, "service_type": "product", "qty": 2, "variation_id": 5 }` — `variation_id` only applies to a variable product (from Product Detail's `variations` array, or resolve one from picked options via `term_ids: [113, 117]` instead of a known `variation_id`); a simple product only needs `qty`. See Booking > Add to Cart.

item.name: Booking

request.description: App bootstrap config: active languages, every bookable service type + its search form fields, guest-checkout flag, currency, and enabled social logins. No auth required.

Available payment gateways (logo, name, description, any extra form fields) to render at Checkout. **Requires the Login Bearer token** (not actually public despite how this might read — it isn't in the controller's unauthenticated-route exceptions).

`is_offline` and `supports_cart` matter for the Cart & Checkout folder: only a gateway with `supports_cart: true` (or `is_offline: true`) can be passed as `payment_gateway` to Cart & Checkout's Checkout — anything else is rejected there with a clear error rather than silently failing.

response.name: 200 — Success

request.description:
Creates a draft booking and adds it to the cart. Returns `booking_code` on success — pass that as `code` to Checkout.

**Required:** `service_id`, `service_type` (`tour`), `start_date` (`Y-m-d`, must fall within Tour Availability's results), and either `guests` (simple pricing) or `person_types` (if the tour has per-person-type pricing — check Tour Detail's `person_types` field to know which applies). Optional: `extra_price[<key>][enable]` for add-ons the tour offers.

Requires: logged in (registered) **and** verified email — the two things this app now enforces before anyone can book. You can't book your own tour if you happen to be its author.

**Car booking uses a different shape**: instead of a single `start_date` + `guests`/`person_types`, a car's Add to Cart takes a rental **date range** — `start_date` + `end_date` (both `Y-m-d`, must fall within Car Availability's results) — plus `number` (how many of this car, defaults to 1). Just swap `service_type` to `"car"` and the body to `{ "service_id": 1, "service_type": "car", "start_date": "2026-09-01", "end_date": "2026-09-04", "number": 1 }`.

**Event booking uses a different shape too**: this site runs `event_booking_type = "ticket"` (an admin setting), so an event's Add to Cart takes `start_date` (must fall within Event Availability's results) plus a `ticket_types` object keyed by **array index** into the event's ticket tiers — e.g. `{ "service_id": 1, "service_type": "event", "start_date": "2026-08-01", "ticket_types": { "0": { "number": 2 }, "1": { "number": 1 } } }` to book 2 of ticket_types[0] and 1 of ticket_types[1]. There's no `guests` field — the ticket quantities themselves determine `total_guests`.

**Product (Shop) booking is the simplest of all**: no dates at all — just `{ "service_id": 16, "service_type": "product", "qty": 2, "variation_id": 5 }`. `variation_id` is required only for a variable product (get it from Product Detail's `variations`, or pass `term_ids: [113, 117]` instead to resolve one from picked options); a simple product just needs `qty`.

item.description:
Booking a tour is a 2-step flow: **Add to Cart** creates a draft booking, then **Checkout** completes it. Every action here except the read-only ones (Booking Detail, Check Checkout Status, Get Gateways, Get Configs) requires the Login Bearer token — **and now also requires a verified email**, matching the same rule enforced at Login. An unverified account with an otherwise-valid token gets a clear `email_not_verified` error at Add to Cart / Checkout rather than being allowed to proceed.

**For a real multi-item purchase with discount codes, use the Cart & Checkout folder instead** — Checkout here only ever pays for one booking at a time and has no coupon support.

item.name: Cart & Checkout

query.description: Optional — preview a discount without applying it (nothing is stored server-side)

request.description:
Your cart is simply your own draft bookings — every Add to Cart call (Tour/Car/Event/Guide.../Shop, all under the Booking folder) already stamps `customer_id`, so there's no separate "create a cart" step and no session involved. Add items from any module's Add to Cart, then they show up here regardless of which endpoint added them.

Pass `coupon_code` to preview a discount for informational display — it is **not** remembered by the server; pass the same code again at Checkout to actually apply it.

request.description: Validates a coupon code against the cart's live subtotal (status, expiry date, min/max order total, per-user restriction) and returns the resulting discount. Same as Get Cart's `coupon_code` param, just a dedicated endpoint with a clearer success/error message — nothing is persisted either way, so still pass `coupon_code` again at Checkout.

Quantity change for a **product** cart item only (`item_id` is the `id` field from Get Cart's `items`, not the product id) — other item types don't have a quantity to change. `qty: 0` removes the item, same as Remove from Cart. Re-validates stock before saving.
`item_id` is the `id` field from Get Cart's `items` (a booking id, not the tour/car/product id). Deletes the draft booking outright.

Groups **every** item currently in the cart into one order and pays for it in a single transaction (all-or-nothing — if any one item fails its own availability/stock check, nothing is charged). `coupon_code` is optional and, unlike Get Cart's preview, is actually applied and snapshotted onto the order here.

`payment_gateway` must be one of Get Payment Gateways' keys with `is_offline: true` or `supports_cart: true` — anything else is rejected with a clear error rather than silently mis-charging.

**Two different response shapes depending on the gateway:**
- **Offline** (e.g. `"offline"`): the order is paid immediately. `status` comes back `"processing"`, the cart is already empty, and there's nothing further to do — fetch the receipt via Order Detail whenever you want it.
- **Online/redirect** (e.g. `"moyasar"`): the order comes back `"unpaid"` and a `payment` object is included — open `payment.url` in a webview to let the customer actually pay. The cart is NOT cleared yet (items are parked, not deleted, so they can't be double-checked-out while payment is in flight). You do **not** need to handle `payment.success_url`/`cancel_url` yourselves beyond closing the webview when navigation reaches them — just poll Order Detail afterward for the authoritative status; it lazily re-verifies with the gateway itself while the order is still `unpaid`, so it's correct even if the webview's own redirect never lands.

response.name: 200 — Unsupported gateway for combined cart

request.description:
The receipt — the order totals plus every item it grouped (same shape as Get Cart's `items`, but now each one's `total` reflects what it was actually charged, and the items are no longer drafts). Scoped to the logged-in user; another account's order code returns "Order not found", not someone else's data.

**If the order was paid through an online gateway, this call is also how you find out it succeeded.** While `order.status` is still `"unpaid"`, every call here re-verifies with the gateway itself before responding — so polling this endpoint after closing the payment webview is sufficient even if the webview's own redirect back never actually reached the server. `payment_error` is set (and the items are released back into the cart) if the payment failed or was cancelled instead.
Order history — a summary row per order (not the full receipt; call Order Detail with each `code` for that).

item.description:
The recommended way to actually complete a purchase — groups everything a customer has added to their cart (from any module's Add to Cart: Tour, Car, Event, Shop, ...) into one combined order with one coupon and one receipt.

**Why this exists as its own folder, separate from Booking's older Checkout**: the web app's cart/coupon state normally lives in a PHP session, which a Bearer-token mobile client can never reach (confirmed directly — Sanctum only starts a session for requests carrying an Origin/Referer header, which a native app never sends, so no session cookie is ever returned). These endpoints instead treat "the cart" as simply the customer's own draft bookings and take the coupon code explicitly on each call rather than remembering one server-side — same underlying checkout/discount logic as the web cart, just reached statelessly. Booking's single-item Checkout still works standalone if you ever need to pay for exactly one item outside the cart flow, but it has no discount support and produces its own separate per-item receipt instead of one combined order.

**Online (redirect) gateways are supported here too** (e.g. Moyasar) — not just offline ones. See the Checkout request below for the shape that unlocks: instead of an immediate receipt, you get a `payment.url` to open in a webview. Check Get Payment Gateways' `supports_cart` field to know which gateways can be used for a combined-cart checkout at all.
